---
title: Requirements and capabilities
---

**laplacekit** never looks at a model's class or its attribute names to decide what to do.
It runs the model through autograd and records what works.
A method says what it needs, and the two are compared before any data goes into the fit.
That way, a long pass over the data never ends in an error that the first batch could have shown.

## The probe

`lk.core.probe(model, likelihood, batch, params=...)` runs the model on the first two examples of a batch and returns a `Capabilities` object.
One forward pass under `no_grad` records `module_order` (the modules that own parameters, in the order their forward finished), `hooked` (the `Linear` and `Conv2d` modules whose forward hooks fire) and `event_size`, and `tied` lists the tied weights.
Then it tries `vjp`, `jvp` and `vmap` through `torch.func`, and `vjp_twice`, the VJP of a VJP, which must also agree with the plain VJP.
Each one is tried on its own.
`caps.failures` keeps the first line of each error:

```python
caps = lk.core.probe(lk.core.ModelFn.from_module(model), lk.Categorical(), batch)

caps.vjp_twice      # False for fused attention kernels
caps.failures       # {"vjp_twice": "RuntimeError: ..."}
```

`lk.laplace` probes twice on the first batch.
The first probe, with `subset={}`, records the forward order, which the subset reads.
The second runs on the chosen parameters only, so the rest of the model is never differentiated.

## Requirements

A curvature, a `Staged` method or a predictive states its needs in `requires`:

```python
@property
def requires(self) -> lk.core.Requirements:
    return lk.core.Requirements(vjp=True, vmap=True, needs_output_hessian=True)
```

The model needs are `vjp`, `vjp_twice`, `jvp`, `vmap` and `hooks` (the module types whose forward hooks must fire).
`one_of` takes alternatives, at least one of which must hold.
The [Predictives](predictive.py) guide uses it for "a JVP or a VJP".
The data needs are `needs_targets`, `weights` and `input_type`.
The likelihood needs are `needs_sample`, `needs_distribution`, `needs_output_hessian` and `late_scale`; the [Curvatures](curvature.py#requirements-and-capabilities) guide explains each.

Right after the probe, before the method sees a batch, `lk.laplace` calls `caps.check(requires, name)` and `check_likelihood(requires, likelihood, name)`.
`requires.check_batch` then runs on the first batch, and again on every batch the method sees.
For an explicit `hessian_approx=`, the likelihood check runs before even the first batch is drawn.
Each failure is a `CapabilityError` that names the method, what is missing, and why the probe said no:

```text
HutchinsonDiag(n_probes=16) needs vjp (RuntimeError: ...), which this model does not support
```

## What `Requirements` can't say

Some needs aren't capabilities, e.g., "a `Categorical` likelihood only".
For those, a method gets a `FitContext` in `init` (or `plan`, for `Staged`), before any data, and raises `CapabilityError` there.
A subset raises `StructureError` or `CapabilityError` when it can't select anything, since it also runs before the fit.
To test what an object is, use `isinstance` on a type or a runtime-checkable protocol, never `hasattr`.

Priors follow the same rule.
Before the first batch, `lk.laplace` asks the hyper tuner to check the prior (`HyperTuner.check`).
The built-in tuners check `prior.tunable()`: the tensors must be positive and must be leaves of the prior itself, else `StructureError`.
`lk.GridSearch` with a prior that is not a `TunablePrior` raises the same error, also before any data.

::: {.callout-note}
By hand, `lk.core.fit_curvature(model, likelihood, params, method, capabilities=caps)` always checks the likelihood needs, but it checks the model needs only when it gets `caps`.
Without them, nothing has been probed.
:::
